transcript.content: Hi, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… I came because at work, I keep hearing these voices, like from the call-light speaker and sometimes the hallway vents. They’ll say things about which patient records got changed, like they know. And it’s clear—like someone’s standing right next to me talking.

But then the unit will be quiet, you know, that weird quiet after everyone’s finally settled, and nobody else hears it. I asked once, kind of casually, because I didn’t want to sound… anyway, they looked at me like I was just hearing the air system. But it’s not just air. It’s words.
Before these voices started, had you recently had a medical illness, head injury, seizure, or started using any drugs or new medications?

I don’t… I mean, I don’t think so? I didn’t hit my head or anything that I can remember. No seizure that I know of. As far as being sick, I work around sick people all the time, so it’s hard to say what counts, you know? Sometimes you feel run-down and keep going because the floor is short-staffed.

New medications… I’d have to think. I don’t think there was anything big, but I’m not always great at remembering exact timing. And drugs, no—well, I don’t know what you mean exactly, like street drugs? No, not that.
How long have you been hearing these voices?

About two months, I think. It kind of started around when they asked me to help lead that wound-care documentation rollout at work—which was supposed to be simple, but of course it turned into all these meetings and people acting like I was responsible for every little charting mistake. So… yeah, about two months.
Have you noticed your thoughts becoming jumbled or hard to keep track of?

Yes… yes, that’s actually been happening a lot. It’s like my mind won’t stay on one thing. I’ll be thinking about wound measurements, then patient initials, then the dates on the forms, then what it all means, and suddenly it’s like I’ve got ten tabs open in my head and none of them will close.

And then I’ll remember something from another chart, or like—this one patient’s daughter who always brings those little peppermint candies, which is not even the point, but it all connects somehow in my head and I can’t slow it down enough to sort it out.
Have there been times when you felt unusually confused or not fully alert?

I don’t know… confused like what, exactly? I mean, sometimes I lose track of what I’m doing, but then everybody does when there’s too much going on. Like at work, if three call lights are going off and someone’s family member is asking about laundry, and then you’re trying to remember who needed thickened liquids—sorry, that’s not what you asked.

Not fully alert… I don’t think I’ve been, like, out of it. I’m awake. I know where I am. I just get… scattered, maybe. It’s hard to tell the difference sometimes.
Have these voices been present for at least one month?

Yes—yeah, definitely more than a month. It’s been about two months now, since that wound-care documentation rollout thing at work started, when they asked me to help lead it. I keep thinking if they hadn’t put me in the middle of all those forms and meetings… but yes, about two months.
Do you believe someone is deliberately sending these voices to you or trying to control or monitor you?

I don’t know if “sending” is the right word… but yes, I do think they’re watching. Like, the wound-care charts, they show a pattern, and management doesn’t want anyone noticing it.

My supervisor keeps saying it’s just late entries, coding mistakes, normal paperwork problems—she says that like it’s supposed to make me drop it. But I can tell they’re paying attention to what I write now because I’m the one who caught it. I mean, why else would they be so focused on my notes? And the forms changed right after—well, not right after, but around then—and that’s not nothing.
Have you had a period of feeling unusually high or energized?

Yeah… some days I do. It’s like I’m finally awake, like everybody else has been half-asleep about what’s going on at work and I’m the one who can fix it if they’d just let me.

And then if my husband says, “Maybe take a break,” or one of the nurses tells me to slow down, I just— I snap. I get so mad because it feels like they’re blocking something important, like they don’t understand there’s a reason I’m moving fast. I know I probably sound difficult when I say that, but in the moment it feels urgent.
Have you needed much less sleep than usual lately?

I… I’m not really sure how to answer that. My sleep’s been kind of all over the place, but I don’t know if I’d say I “needed less,” exactly. Some nights I just end up thinking about things, and then suddenly it’s late, and then there’s work the next day and the whole schedule gets messed up.

My husband would probably have an opinion about it—he always notices if I’m up doing things or moving around—but I haven’t really kept track, you know? So… I don’t know. Maybe? I’m not sure.
Have you been more active than usual, starting lots of projects or doing much more than you normally would?

Yes… I mean, I guess I have been doing more. After a full shift, when most people would probably just go home and sit down, I get in and I’m cleaning the kitchen, sorting through supplies, rewriting my notes so they’re clearer—because if the notes aren’t right, then later people act like you didn’t say what you said.

And my husband will be standing there saying, “Please just sit for a minute,” and I’m pacing around the kitchen, moving things from one place to another. It doesn’t feel like “projects” exactly, it feels like there’s just so much that needs to be handled.
Have other people said you’ve been talking much more than usual, or that they can’t interrupt you?

Yeah… my husband says that. And one of the nurses too, actually. It’s mostly when I start explaining the documentation problem, because people act like it’s just paperwork, but it’s not, it’s how things get twisted later, and then suddenly I can hear myself talking faster and faster.

I know I’m doing it, sort of, but I can’t stop, because if I pause I feel like I’ll lose the whole thread. Like it’ll all fall apart before I get to the important part. So I just keep going, and then people try to jump in, and that makes me start over because they’re missing what I’m trying to say.
Have there been at least 7 days in a row when you felt unusually energized or unusually irritable most of the day?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t know if I counted it like seven days exactly, but there’s been a stretch where most of the day I feel like I’m finally awake, like I can see what needs to be fixed at work and everybody else is just moving too slow.

And then if my husband says, “Calm down,” or one of the nurses tells me to slow down, I just— I snap at them. It feels like they’re blocking something important, like if I stop, it won’t get done right. I know that sounds dramatic, but in the moment it feels very real.
Have the voices and feeling watched ever happened during times when you were not feeling unusually energized or irritable?

No… I don’t think so. Not before all of this.

I mean, I’ve worked around call lights for years, and charts are always a mess in some way—people write things sloppy, or they don’t document what they should, and then everyone acts surprised later. But I never heard them like voices before, and I wasn’t seeing messages hidden in the charts before this whole rollout thing got me so wound up.

It started after I was sleeping less and just going and going, working nonstop, feeling like I had to fix everything at the facility before it got away from us. That’s when the voices and the watched feeling started. Not like… out of nowhere during a calm time.
